title: Some constant variables ( Array Dictionary ) used as default values in function arguments cannot be modified while others can 4.x does not work 3.6 does
body:
### Tested versions

Does not work in any 4.x
v4.5.dev2.official [af2c71397]

Works in 3.6 at least
v3.6.stable.official [de2f0f147]



### System information

Godot v4.5.dev2 - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 10 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6636) - 11th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-11900K @ 3.50GHz (16 threads)

### Issue description

I use constants as my default values, but in some functions I will reassign that argument value, but as of 4.x Arrays and Dictionaries cannot be assigned. I am not sure why, but only recently noticed it when testing some of my older scripts. The example script shows what I mean.

Output of 3.6:
```
int
Before	0
After	123

float
Before	0
After	123.456

String
Before	
After	Changed

Array
Before	[]
After	[Changed]

Dictionary
Before	{}
After	{Changed:123.456}

```

Output of 4.x:
```
int
Before	0
After	123

float
Before	0.0
After	123.456

String
Before	
After	Changed

Array
Before	[]
After	[]

Dictionary
Before	{  }
```
With 2 debug errors saying that the Array and Dictionary are in read-only state. Also a stack trace for the Dictionary with:
`Invalid assignment on read-only value (on base:'Dictionary').`

Another thing to note is that the dictionary in 4.x is not {} but instead { }



### Steps to reproduce

Add a control node with this script:

```gdscript
extends Control

#Types only in 4.x
#const BLANK_PACKED_BYTE :PackedByteArray= []
#const BLANK_PACKED_INT32 :PackedInt32Array= []
#const BLANK_PACKED_INT64 :PackedInt64Array= []
#const BLANK_PACKED_FLOAT32 :PackedFloat32Array= []
#const BLANK_PACKED_FLOAT64 :PackedFloat64Array= []
#const BLANK_PACKED_STRING :PackedStringArray= []
#Types in 4.x and 3.6
const BLANK_INT :int= 0
const BLANK_FLOAT :float= 0.0
const BLANK_STRING :String= ""
const BLANK_ARRAY :Array= []
const BLANK_DICT :Dictionary= {}

func _ready() -> void:
	test_assign()

func test_assign(
	#Works in 4.x
	#arg_packed_byte :PackedByteArray= BLANK_PACKED_BYTE,
	#arg_packed_int32 :PackedInt32Array= BLANK_PACKED_INT32,
	#arg_packed_int64 :PackedInt64Array= BLANK_PACKED_INT64,
	#arg_packed_float32 :PackedFloat32Array= BLANK_PACKED_FLOAT32,
	#arg_packed_float64 :PackedFloat64Array= BLANK_PACKED_FLOAT64,
	#arg_packed_string :PackedStringArray= BLANK_PACKED_STRING,
	#Works in 4.x and 3.6
	arg_int :int= BLANK_INT,
	arg_float :float= BLANK_FLOAT,
	arg_string :String= BLANK_STRING,
	#Does not work in 4.x but works in 3.6
	arg_array :Array= BLANK_ARRAY,
	arg_dict :Dictionary= BLANK_DICT
) -> void:
	#print("PackedByteArray")
	#printt("Before",arg_packed_byte)
	#arg_packed_byte.append(123)
	#printt("After",arg_packed_byte)
	#print()
	#
	#print("PackedInt32Array")
	#printt("Before",arg_packed_int32)
	#arg_packed_int32.append(123)
	#printt("After",arg_packed_int32)
	#print()
	#
	#print("PackedInt64Array")
	#printt("Before",arg_packed_int64)
	#arg_packed_int64.append(123)
	#printt("After",arg_packed_int64)
	#print()
	#
	#print("PackedFloat32Array")
	#printt("Before",arg_packed_float32)
	#arg_packed_float32.append(123.456)
	#printt("After",arg_packed_float32)
	#print()
	#
	#print("PackedFloat64Array")
	#printt("Before",arg_packed_float64)
	#arg_packed_float64.append(123.456)
	#printt("After",arg_packed_float64)
	#print()
	#
	#print("PackedStringArray")
	#printt("Before",arg_packed_string)
	#arg_packed_string.append("Changed")
	#printt("After",arg_packed_string)
	#print()
	
	print("int")
	printt("Before",arg_int)
	arg_int = 123
	printt("After",arg_int)
	print()
	
	print("float")
	printt("Before",arg_float)
	arg_float = 123.456
	printt("After",arg_float)
	print()
	
	print("String")
	printt("Before",arg_string)
	arg_string = "Changed"
	printt("After",arg_string)
	print()
	
	print("Array")
	printt("Before",arg_array)
	arg_array.append("Changed")
	printt("After",arg_array)
	#printerr("Array is in read-only state.") # 4.x debugger error
	print()
	
	print("Dictionary")
	printt("Before",arg_dict)
	arg_dict["Changed"] = 123.456
	printt("After",arg_dict)
	#printerr("Invalid assignment on read-only value (on base:'Dictionary').") # 4.x stack error
	print()

```
